concerns.text: T031a mandates fetching human pilot data from a specific external HuggingFace URL (`huggingface.co/datasets/edu-pilot-math`) and exits with code 1 if unavailable. This violates Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) which forbids reliance on external manual interventions or unavailable external sources for core experimental data. The spec (FR-010) requires calibration against human data, but the task fails to provide a reproducible mechanism (e.g., a synthetic generator or a verified, permanent public dataset) to produce this data on a fresh runner, effectively blocking the pipeline if the external source is removed.

T031c provides instructions for manual upload of pilot data if the automated fetch fails. This directly contradicts Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) which states 'Every result... MUST be reproducible by re-running the project's code/... on a fresh GitHub Actions runner' and 'Every notebook or script under code/ is runnable end-to-end without manual intervention.' Relying on manual intervention for a blocking prerequisite (calibration) is a constitutional violation.

T012c implements the fetch for the Khan Academy dataset but lacks the explicit timeout enforcement and error message logic required by FR-007 and SC-008. While T012 (ASSISTments) includes the specific error message 'ERROR: Failed to download [dataset name] within 300 seconds – aborting pipeline.', T012c only mentions using `datasets.load_dataset` without defining the timeout handling or the exact error string. This is a semantic weakening of FR-007 for the second required dataset.

T023 implements a validation check that blocks the simulation pipeline if response time gaps > 5s are found. SC-005 describes this as a quality metric for the final data distribution ('no gaps larger than 5 s'), but T023 treats it as a hard blocker for the *generation* phase. Since the BKT simulation is probabilistic, it may naturally produce sparse distributions that fail this check, causing the pipeline to stall indefinitely. The task weakens the feasibility of the simulation by enforcing a data-quality constraint as a generation blocker without a mechanism to adjust the simulation parameters or retry.

T064 (Wolfram Rule Space Search) implements an agent-based model to search for simple rewriting rules. This task has no trace to any Functional Requirement (FR) or Success Criterion (SC) in the spec. It introduces significant computational complexity and scope creep that is not mandated by the research question or the spec, violating the constraint that tasks must not introduce unverified empirical values or scope beyond the plan.

The tasks for pilot data (T031a, T031b, T031c) create a circular dependency on an external, unverified source (`edu-pilot-math`) for a mandatory requirement (FR-010). The spec (FR-010) requires calibration against human data, but the tasks do not define a reproducible way to obtain this data (e.g., a synthetic generator as hinted in the Plan's T030a, or a verified public dataset). This leaves the project unable to satisfy FR-010 on a fresh runner, violating Constitution Principle I.
